summary: StarBound is an interactive space experience that tells the stories of robotic explorers that once ventured across the Moon, Mars, and our Solar System. Explore their missions, discoveries, final moments, and the science they left behind through an immersive, kid-friendly experience that turns spacecraft history into stories and games worth remembering. It also contains a deeper archive that reveals a complete legacy of these missions through storybooks, simulations, and mapping. Finally, it will create a community of curious students who can work on recovering, servicing, and preserving these abandoned space objects by sharing their ideas and coming up with innovations.
details:
Space exploration is usually remembered through historic launches, groundbreaking discoveries, and successful missions. But what about the explorers that stopped communicating, became stranded, or reached the end of their missions? Their journeys may have ended, but the scientific knowledge they gathered remains valuable.

StarBound is an interactive space-exploration and storytelling platform that preserves the stories of abandoned robotic explorers across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, it transforms scattered mission information and technical records into an engaging experience where users can discover these explorers, understand their scientific contributions, revisit their final moments, and explore possibilities for their future.

What does it do and how does it work?

StarBound offers two interconnected experiences designed for different audiences:

  • Kids Mode: Makes space exploration accessible to younger audiences through illustrated explorer stories, an interactive rover game, and 3D rover anatomy that introduces the different components of robotic explorers.
  • Adult Mode: Provides a deeper exploration experience through detailed mission storybooks, a 3D simulation console, interactive rover anatomy, and an interactive Moon and Mars map. Users can explore abandoned space objects, examine their locations through a timeline, learn about their missions and discoveries, and understand where and why their journeys ended.

Each explorer has a dedicated story covering its origin, mission objectives, scientific achievements, and final status. The platform also includes a community-driven Recovery Ideas section, where users can propose ways to recover, service, or preserve abandoned explorers. Contributors can share their ideas, expected impacts, and potential drawbacks, allowing others to explore different approaches.

Looking beyond the present, Mender represents our future-facing recovery-system concept: an exploration of how inactive or stranded robotic explorers might one day be inspected, serviced, and potentially recovered. Mender is a conceptual vision, not a currently operational or implemented recovery system.

Benefits and Intended Impact

StarBound addresses the gap between the enormous scientific value of historic space missions and the difficulty of accessing their stories through conventional technical archives.

Its intended impact includes:

  • Preserving scientific legacy: Bringing mission histories, discoveries, and final known locations together in one accessible experience.
  • Making STEM education engaging: Introducing younger audiences to planetary science, robotics, engineering, and space exploration through interactive storytelling and gameplay.
  • Improving access to scientific information: Presenting complex mission records in a more understandable and visually engaging format.
  • Encouraging innovation: Giving students and space enthusiasts a platform to propose ideas for recovering, servicing, and preserving abandoned space equipment.
  • Inspiring future exploration: Encouraging people to look beyond how spacecraft are launched and operated, and consider what happens to them after their missions end.

Our goal is not simply to document abandoned explorers, but to inspire a generation to value their contributions and imagine what could be possible next.

Tools, Technologies, and Data Sources

StarBound was developed as a web application using:

  • React, TypeScript, and Vite: Core application architecture and development.
  • Tailwind CSS: Responsive styling and interface design.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber: Interactive 3D visualizations and rover models.
  • Framer Motion: Animations and interactive transitions.
  • MapLibre GL and PMTiles: Interactive lunar and Martian maps and geospatial visualization.
  • Firebase (optional): Community recovery-idea submissions and storage.

We used authoritative NASA and planetary-science resources to ground the experience in actual mission information:

  • NASA/JPL Photojournal: Mission photographs and explorer imagery.
  • NASA Image and Video Library: Historical mission visuals.
  • NSSDCA Master Catalog: Space-object identities and mission dates.
  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS): Planetary-object coordinates.
  • NASA Trek: Lunar and Martian map basemaps.
  • HiRISE: Mars imagery and coordinate references.
  • NASA/JPL 3D resources: Rover models and 3D content.

These sources help connect the interactive experience to documented mission histories and scientific records rather than relying entirely on fictional storytelling.

Creativity and Design Considerations

Our central creative idea was to change how people perceive abandoned space equipment. Instead of treating these explorers as obsolete machines, we approached them as explorers whose journeys deserve to be remembered.

We combined scientific archives with interactive storytelling, educational gameplay, 3D visualization, geospatial exploration, and community participation. The two-mode design considers different levels of technical familiarity and age groups, allowing younger visitors to learn through play while providing more detailed exploration for users interested in mission history and technology.

We also prioritized historical accuracy, traceable data sources, accessibility, and clear distinctions between documented mission facts and speculative future possibilities. The experience is designed to remain engaging without compromising the scientific significance of the missions.

StarBound's central belief is simple: a spacecraft does not lose the value of its discoveries just because it can no longer communicate with Earth. Its mission may have ended, but its contribution to humanity's understanding of the universe remains.

THE SIGNAL MAY HAVE ENDED. THE STORY HASN'T.
